subject: CloudBurst usage bands & cost modeling — pilot quote and next steps
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Claire Zhang <claire@cloudburst.ai>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Oct 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Recap: CloudBurst call — usage bands & next steps

Claire — great to meet you on the call today. Quick recap and the asks we agreed on so we have a shared starting point. I attached a simple modeling workbook (CloudBurst_Usage_Modeling.xlsx) that mirrors the numbers below.

Summary of the three primary workloads you described:
- Search augmentation (short prompts, KV cache hit expected): baseline 120M tokens/mo, seasonal bursts to 350M
- Long-form summarization (avg 600 tokens/req): baseline 45M tokens/mo, up to 150M at peak
- Customer support synthesis (mixed length): baseline 35M tokens/mo, spikes to 250M during campaigns

Aggregate baseline: ~200M tokens/mo (projected steady-state month 3)
Aggregate peak burst window: ~1.2B tokens in a heavy month (marketing launch scenario)

Budget guidance you provided on the call: $40k–$70k/month initially; procurement prefers a pilot-first path and wants to see a clean unit economics story. You asked us to target a reference unit around $/1M tokens for planning — you mentioned comfort around $500–$750/1M for the pilot.

What Redwood will deliver next:
1) A short invoice-style estimate showing three options (hosted PAYG, short pilot commit, 12-month reserved) with per-1M token unit prices and total month estimates for baseline and peak months. (Aditya will send this.)
2) A cost breakdown tab in the attached workbook showing model runtime assumptions (seq lengths, quantization impact, caching hit-rate) so you can see sensitivity to prompt length.
3) SOC2 + audit packet and contract/PO path details for your procurement team (Marcus will own this).

Immediate asks for you:
- Confirm the three workload buckets above and the baseline/peak numbers (or attach your monthly export if you want us to use exacts)
- Confirm the budget range that would get you to sign a pilot (is $40–70k/month still the right band?)
- If procurement will require an approved vendor form or specific SOC2 artifacts, can you share the intake doc or contact?

Attachments: CloudBurst_Usage_Modeling.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)

Thanks — will follow up with the formal estimate tomorrow.

—
Soojin Lee
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.com
redwood.com
From: Claire Zhang <claire@cloudburst.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@cloudburst.ai
Date: Fri, 30 Oct 2026 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap: CloudBurst call — usage bands & next steps

Soojin — thanks for the clear recap. Confirming the three buckets and the baseline/peak figures look right for internal planning. A couple of quick points: 

- For the pilot we were hoping to land closer to $500/1M tokens if possible for the first 3–6 months (volume commitment limited) — that would make the math clean for our CFO. If you can illustrate a path to that price via optimization + commit, that would be ideal.
- Procurement will ask for SOC2 Type II and standard SLAs. I’ve CC'd procurement@cloudburst.ai who will share the vendor intake form.
- Timeline: we'd like a pilot quote by end of next week and procurement sign-off within 3 weeks of the quote (if numbers align).

I attached the signed NDA we used on the call.

—
Claire Zhang
Head of Product, CloudBurst.ai
claire@cloudburst.ai

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Claire Zhang <claire@cloudburst.ai>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 31 Oct 2026 07:02:00 -0700
Subject: Redwood estimate for CloudBurst — pilot & reserved options (invoice style)

Claire — following up with the estimate we discussed. I’m attaching a compact invoice-style PDF (redwood_estimate_cloudburst_v3.pdf) and included the key lines inline so you can copy into procurement. The attached spreadsheet from Soojin has the modeling tabs; I added a sensitivity tab that shows how quantization and caching move the unit economics.

Key assumptions behind these numbers (in the attached workbook): average prompt length per workload, KV cache hit 28% on search, 20% long-form reuse on summaries, 8 GPU-second cost basis normalized per 1M tokens (internal compute model). We can share the runtime trace if you want deeper detail.

Pricing options (USD per 1M tokens)
- Option A — Hosted PAYG (no commit): $1,100 / 1M tokens
- Option B — 3-month pilot commit (10M tokens minimum total): $900 / 1M tokens (applies to committed volume)
- Option C — 12-month reserved (predictable, SLA-backed): $700 / 1M tokens (tiered discounts beyond 100M/mo)

Optimization path to Claire's $500 target:
- Using model quantization + small architectural swap (recommended for long-form summarization) we estimate ~20–30% lower per-token execution cost.
- Combined with a staged commit (pilot -> reserve) we can get effective blended price down to ~$550–600 / 1M tokens within 2 quarters for the workloads you described. Hitting $500 would require either a larger 12-month commit or a co-engineering agreement on model variant tuning.

Invoice-style example for month 3 (steady-state baseline 200M tokens):
- Option A (PAYG): 200 * $1,100 = $220,000
- Option B (Pilot at $900/1M): 200 * $900 = $180,000 (if committed volume covers it; otherwise blended)
- Option C (Reserve at $700/1M): 200 * $700 = $140,000

Peak month example (1.2B tokens): multiply same unit prices — we'll provide burst handling options (burst at PAYG over commit, or temporary burst credits under a reserved contract).

Attachments: redwood_estimate_cloudburst_v3.pdf (invoice format)
Drive link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2bCloudBurstModeling (sensitivity workbook)
HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/CB-2026-0931

Next steps I propose:
1) Soojin: finalize the formal quote PDF and send a version with line-item totals for procurement.
2) Claire / procurement: send vendor intake form and expected PO timing.
3) Marcus: send SOC2 artifacts and a short one-pager on SLAs & data controls.

Happy to hop on another 30-minute call if you want to walk the numbers with finance.

—
Aditya Rao
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwood.com
From: Claire Zhang <claire@cloudburst.ai>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@cloudburst.ai
Date: Sat, 31 Oct 2026 09:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood estimate for CloudBurst — pilot & reserved options (invoice style)

Aditya / Soojin — thanks for the clear breakdown. Procurement confirms they can accept a 3-month pilot PO if we get pricing near $850/1M for the first quarter (blended), and then move to the reserved $700 band on a 12-month commit. That blended ask moves us closer to internal go/no-go.

Next items from our side:
- Procurement will send the vendor intake form by EOD Monday (I CC'd them here).
- We want the formal quote (PO-ready) with line item totals, tax fields, and payment instructions. Can you send that by COB Monday so internal approval can happen on Tuesday?
- We also want the SOC2 Type II report and the contact for legal to run a short review.

If you can put the three pricing options in a single PDF and include the pilot blended example at $850/1M, that will match what procurement needs to approve the pilot PO.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — we should be able to move fast if the numbers align.

—
Claire Zhang
Head of Product, CloudBurst.ai
